purpose: Review the cited FAO Sciaenidae account for Johnius borneensis to determine whether it supports a cautious, stage-dependent natural-diet research summary. Keep the reference's regional scope and evidence type separate from Pagatpatan prey observations, local occurrence, bait guidance and app publication approval.

studySource.author: Kunio Sasaki
studySource.bookTitle: The Living Marine Resources of the Western Central Pacific
studySource.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

accessAndReuse.visualReview: Downloaded the official FAO PDF part and visually inspected the species-account page; local text extraction independently confirmed the heading Johnius (Johnieops) borneensis and the diet statement on printed page 3154.
accessAndReuse.rightsNote: The volume overview identifies © FAO 2001. FAO's current rights page says publications may generally be reused in non-commercial products or services with attribution unless otherwise indicated, and directs reproduction/adaptation permission requests to its licence form. Because this is a 2001 work and no item-specific license was verified, do not treat the current general policy as a confirmed grant for every use or for a future commercial Bangwit service.
accessAndReuse.decision: Retain an attributed factual research summary and link to the official source. Do not copy the illustration or substantial text. Keep public app reuse pending rights review; no FAO endorsement is implied.

scope.geographicScope: Species account in a Western Central Pacific fisheries identification guide; broader than and not specific to the Philippines, Caraga, Pagatpatan or a named waterbody.
scope.sourceEvidenceType: Secondary/reference species account; page 3154 provides a biological statement but no underlying gut-content dataset, sample sizes, prey counts, season, locality or study method.
scope.crosswalk: The scientific name matches the Pagatpatan 2015 paper's Johnius borneensis; this is a taxon-name match, not a locality, specimen or sample crosswalk.

dietEvidence.sourceStatementSummary: The FAO account says crustaceans are the preferred diet of juveniles and that fishes show a piscivorous tendency as the fish grow.
preyCategories: crustaceans (preferred diet of juveniles, as summarized by the FAO account)
dietEvidence.uncertainty: The reference account does not disclose the underlying diet-study methods or geographic population for this statement. Natural diet may vary by size, habitat, season, and prey availability; it cannot be represented as an invariant menu or a Pagatpatan-specific observation.

limitations: The evidence is a 2001 species account, not a new stomach-content study or quantitative diet dataset.
The guide covers the Western Central Pacific and does not establish the diet of a Caraga or Pagatpatan population.
No prey species, percentages, sampling dates, population, waterbody or feeding method are given on the reviewed account page.
A name match with the 2015 Pagatpatan capture paper does not link the diet statement to those sampled fish.
Natural diet is distinct from angling bait recommendations and catchability.
No current presence, safety, legal catchability, geometry or public app admission is supported by this diet reference.
FAO identifies the volume as © FAO 2001; the applicable item-specific reuse terms for public or commercial app use were not verified.
nextAction: Look for primary gut-content or diet-composition studies for Johnius borneensis and review their samples, life stages, geography, license and locality independently. Keep non-Philippine studies as comparative evidence only, and do not add local diet or bait suggestions without local support.
